# CS 34.2 — Aircraft engine emissions

> [!summary]
> CS 34.2 is one sentence. It requires the aircraft engine to be designed to
> comply with the emissions requirements specified in point 21.A.21 of Part 21.
> It states no emission limit, no operating cycle and no measurement method. The
> chain is the same as for fuel venting until its last link, where it reaches a
> part of ICAO Annex 16 written for turbojet and turbofan engines. CS-34 was
> repealed in May 2025.

## Requirement

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| — | Design the aircraft engine to comply with the applicable emissions requirements as specified in point 21.A.21 of Annex I (Part 21) to Commission Regulation (EU) No 748/2012. | Required |
| **GM1 34.2** | Point 21.A.21 does not list the applicable requirements. It refers to point 21.A.20, which asks the applicant to demonstrate compliance with the environmental protection requirements designated by the Agency in accordance with point 21.B.85. The requirements are therefore in point 21.B.85. | Statement |

CS 34.2 addresses the **aircraft engine**. Its sibling [[CS 34.1]] addresses the
aircraft. That is the only difference between the two sentences.

### Where the chain goes

Steps 1 to 5 of the chain are identical to the fuel venting case and are set out
once, in [[CS 34.1]]. CS 34.2 reaches point 21.A.21, then point 21.A.20, then
point 21.B.85, and arrives at the SARPs of ICAO Annex 16 [ext GM1 34.2].

The last link is where the two paragraphs separate. For engine emissions the
relevant part is Volume II Part III, and GM1 21.B.85(a) describes its scope:
"Part III of that volume applies to the aircraft engine emissions certification
for turbojet and turbofan engines intended for the propulsion at subsonic and
supersonic speeds" [ext GM1 21.B.85(a)].

The same GM sets out two applicability categories inside Part III. Standards for
new type and model designs "apply to aircraft engines of a type or model for
which an application for a type certificate was submitted on or after a given
date". Standards for first individual production models turn on the date of
manufacture, and "are minimum requirements for continued production of an
aircraft engine (production cut-off standards)" [ext GM1 21.B.85(a)].

**The vault records the chain and stops there.** ICAO Annex 16 is not an EASA
document and this is a CS-E vault.

### The repeal, and what a TCDS may now say

ED Decision 2025/005/R repealed CS-34 in May 2025. [[CS 34.1]] records the
decision's reasoning. Two of its statements bear directly on the emissions note
that [[CS-E 1000]] and [[AMC E 1020|AMC E 1020(1)]] ask for.

First, a CS-34 reference in a data sheet is not a compliance record: "Current
references to CS-34, CS-36 and CS-CO2 in type-certificate data sheets (TCDSs)
and type-certificate data sheets for noise (TCDSNs) do not constitute records of
compliance with the applicable environmental protection requirements"
[ext ED Decision 2025/005/R].

Second, existing data sheets are not invalidated by that: "This repeal has no
impact whatsoever on existing compliance records in TCDSs and TCDSNs since these
data sheets accurately record compliance with the applicable environmental
protection requirements of ICAO Annex 16" [ext ED Decision 2025/005/R].

What the engine data sheet must carry is set by Part 21. Point 21.A.41 states
that "the engine type-certificate data sheet shall include the record of exhaust
emissions compliance" [ext 21.A.41].

## Bearing on this engine

[[CS-E 1020]] requires a demonstration, by test or analysis or a combination,
that the type design complies with the emission specifications of CS 34.2 in
effect at the date of engine certification. CS 34.2 carries no specification, so
the demonstration is against whatever the Agency designates under point
21.B.85(a).

[VERIFY: whether CS-E 1020 reaches this engine at all. GM1 21.B.85(a) states
that Volume II Part III applies to turbojet and turbofan engines, and a
turboshaft is neither. The vault has not changed the applicability verdict on
that basis, because the statement is a GM describing ICAO Annex 16 rather than
Annex 16 itself, and the designation under point 21.B.85(a) is the Agency's act.
Put the question to the Agency early: it decides whether an emissions
demonstration is owed.]

Fuel venting is unaffected by that question. Volume II Part II reaches turbine
engine powered aircraft, as recorded in [[CS 34.1]].

The two applicability categories of Part III match the distinction that
[[AMC E 1020|AMC E 1020(2)]] draws. Type design compliance is fixed by the date
of application; an individual production engine answers to the production
cut-off standard current at its date of manufacture. AMC E 1020(2) states the
same split in CS-E terms.

[VERIFY: the TCDS note format of AMC E 1020(1) reads "Engine (type/model)
complies with CS-34 amendment (number)". ED Decision 2025/005/R says a CS-34
reference in a TCDS is not a record of compliance, and point 21.A.41 asks for
the record of exhaust emissions compliance. Agree the wording of the note with
the Agency before it is drafted.]
